SELECTED_INDEX: 1  
CONFIDENCE: 0.25  
EXPLANATION: Strong twin C–H stretching bands at 2884 / 2918 cm⁻¹ and the CH₂/CH₃ deformation at 1454 cm⁻¹ indicate a saturated aliphatic molecule.  The cluster of medium-intensity bands between 1000 and 1160 cm⁻¹ (1053, 1134, 1155 cm⁻¹) is characteristic of multiple C–O stretching modes found when both an alcohol C–O and an ether C–O–C group are present; simple hydrocarbons or mono-alcohols would show fewer/ weaker bands in this region.  The additional bands at 813–919 cm⁻¹ match C–O–C skeletal/rocking vibrations often seen in aliphatic ethers. Among the candidates, only molecule 1 (CCOCC(O)CC) contains both an ether linkage and an –OH group in a flexible aliphatic chain, fully accounting for the observed pattern, whereas other candidates lack either the ether (3–5, 7) or the hydroxyl (2, 10) or possess more oxygen functions than suggested by the limited number and intensity of the O-related bands (8, 9). Therefore candidate 1 provides the best structural fit to the experimental Raman spectrum.
